newsitem.title: GERMANY: TENNIS-STEFFI GRAFF SAYS TAX EVASION TRIAL VINDICATES HER.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-STEFFI GRAFF SAYS TAX EVASION TRIAL VINDICATES HER.

text.p: Tennis star Steffi Graf said in a newspaper interview on Friday the trial of her father Peter Graf and a former tax advisor on charges of evading millions of marks in tax had only shown her innocence in the affair.

In an interview with the daily Bild she dismissed remarks by former tax advisor Joachim Eckardt in the week-old trial that she and her mother were informed of a scheme to evade tax in 1991 saying that Eckardt's allegations were only hearsay.

Eckardt, on trial alongside her father for tax evasion, told the state court in Mannheim that Steffi Graf was fully aware since 1991 that he and Peter Graf had been concealing large amounts of her tournament winnings and sponsorship money.

"He (Eckardt) said himself he never informed me about tax matters -- particularly not of such a dubious or controversial nature," said the star, who has consistently protested her innocence in the matter.
Peter Graf, who has spent the last 13 months in custody and faces a 10-year jail sentence if convicted, told the court he had kept his daughter in the dark about her finances.

Eckardt told the court he had heard that another advisor, Horst Schmidt, told him that Steffi and her mother knew about a scheme to avoid paying taxes, she said. But Schmidt denied having said this, she said.
"This conversation never took place," she said. "The prosecutors have examined Schmidt's statements and have come to the conclusion that they do no incriminate me.
"I am entirely convinced that no details can emerge in the trial which could suggest any guilt on my part. After the trial there will hopefully be no doubts about my role in the matter.
"But the huge sensation, the personal details about me and my family, these are a terrible burden and I am defenceless against being exposed to this," the star said.
